examples.en: I typed a command into the computer.

examples.ko: 게임에서 쓸 수 있는 명령어가 많아요.
examples.en: There are many commands you can use in the game.
How do you use this command?
The smartphone understands voice commands.
If you write the command wrong, an error appears.

examples.ko: 개발자는 명령어를 외우지 않고 찾아서 써요.
examples.en: Developers look up commands instead of memorizing them.

explain: '명령어'는 컴퓨터나 기계에게 일을 시키려고 입력하는 말이에요. 사람에게 시키는 '명령'과 달리 컴퓨터, 게임, 프로그램 문맥에서만 쓰고, '명령어를 입력하다/실행하다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: You just type the command on the screen.
phrases.nuance_ko: 컴퓨터에 명령어를 쓸 때 가장 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for typing a command into a computer.

phrases.en: I ran the command in the program.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입력한 명령어가 작동하게 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when making a typed command run.

phrases.en: I looked up the game's list of commands.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쓸 수 있는 명령어를 모아 놓은 것이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collection of the commands you can use.

explain_en: 명령어 is the word you type to make a computer or machine do something. Unlike '명령', an order given to a person, it is used only in computer, game and program contexts, as in '명령어를 입력하다'.

t90.ax: How do you use this command?

examples.ko: 위가 음식을 소화하는 데 시간이 걸려요.
examples.en: The stomach takes time to digest food.
Yesterday was hard because I got through the whole schedule.

examples.ko: 이 옷은 키 큰 사람만 소화할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only tall people can pull off this outfit.
The baby can't digest meat yet.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 어려운 역할을 잘 소화했어요.
examples.en: The actor handled the difficult role well.

examples.ko: 이 많은 숙제를 하루에 다 소화하기는 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard to get through all this homework in one day.

explain: 음식을 소화하는 것 말고도 많은 일정이나 어려운 역할, 눈에 띄는 옷을 잘 해내는 것에도 써요. 몸 이야기가 아니면 '해내다'와 비슷한 느낌이에요.

phrases.example: 이번 주에는 일정을 다 소화하기 어려워요.
phrases.en: to get through a schedule
phrases.nuance_ko: 해야 할 일이 많을 때 그 일을 끝까지 해낸다는 뜻으로 써요. 음식 이야기가 아니에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when there is a lot to do and you manage to complete it all. It has nothing to do with food.

explain_en: Besides digesting food, it is also used for getting through a heavy schedule, handling a hard role, or pulling off a bold outfit. When it is not about the body, it feels close to 해내다.

t90.ax: The baby can't digest meat yet.

en: to catch; to get; to comprehend

examples.ko: 선생님 말씀이 너무 빨라서 알아먹기가 어려워요.
examples.en: The teacher speaks so fast that it's hard to follow.
If you got what I said, start right away.
The manual is hard and I can't make out any of it.
My younger sibling is quick-witted and catches on right away.
At first I couldn't understand the dialect.
I only just got the joke my friend made.

explain: '알아먹다'는 '알아듣다'를 편하게 말하는 구어체예요. 친구나 가족끼리 쓰고, 면접이나 발표 같은 공식 자리에서는 '이해하다', '알아듣다'가 더 알맞아요. '못 알아먹겠다'처럼 부정으로 자주 써요.

phrases.en: They talk so fast that I can't understand.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 가장 자주 쓰고 이해가 안 될 때 편하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common negative form, used casually when you can't follow.

phrases.en: My friend asked, "Did you get what I said?"
phrases.nuance_ko: 친한 사이에서 쓰는 반말 질문이에요. 윗사람에게는 쓰지 않아요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual question for close friends; not for elders.

phrases.example: 동생은 한 번만 말해도 잘 알아먹어요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling gets it even if I say it only once.
phrases.nuance_ko: '잘'을 붙여 이해가 빠르다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 잘 means someone catches on quickly.

explain_en: 알아먹다 is the casual, spoken version of 알아듣다. Friends and family use it, while in interviews or presentations 이해하다 or 알아듣다 fits better. It is often used in the negative, like 못 알아먹겠다.

t90.ax: I only just got the joke my friend made.

examples.ko: 오늘 작업량이 너무 많아서 야근해야 해요.
examples.en: Today's workload is so big that I have to work overtime.
The team members split the workload among themselves.
There aren't enough people for the amount of work.
This week's workload is smaller than last week's.
I can't manage the workload, so it's hard.
The workload suddenly doubled.

explain: 사무 일에는 '업무량'을 쓰고, 작업량은 공장, 공사, 편집처럼 직접 손으로 하는 작업에 더 잘 어울려요. '작업량이 많다/적다', '작업량을 줄이다'로 써요.

phrases.en: My workload has increased this month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사무 일에서는 '작업량'보다 '업무량'을 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For office work, this is used more than the headword.

phrases.en: We hired more hands and reduced the workload.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일의 양을 적게 만들 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for making the amount of work smaller.

phrases.en: I decide on a daily workload and work from it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하루에 해야 할 일의 양을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for how much work is to be done in a day.

explain_en: For office work people use '업무량', and '작업량' fits hands-on jobs such as factory work, construction and editing better. Say '작업량이 많다/적다' and '작업량을 줄이다'.

en: to change one's major; to get transferred

examples.en: I switched to the business department in my second year.
To change your major, you need good grades.

examples.ko: 친구가 적성에 안 맞아서 전과하고 싶대요.
examples.en: My friend says he wants to switch majors because it doesn't suit him.

examples.ko: 전과한 뒤에는 새로 배울 게 많았어요.
examples.en: After I switched majors, there was a lot of new material to learn.
My older sister will switch from medicine to law.

examples.ko: 전과하는 학생은 학기 초에 신청해야 해요.
examples.en: Students who transfer departments must apply at the start of the semester.

explain: 대학교에서 다니던 학과를 다른 학과로 바꾸는 일을 말해요. 학교에서만 쓰는 말이라서 '과를 바꾸다'로도 말해요. 비슷하지만 '전공을 바꾸다'는 공부 분야 자체를 바꾼다는 느낌이고, '전과'는 학교에 정식으로 신청하는 절차라는 느낌이 있어요. 같은 소리의 '전과'(범죄 기록)와는 다른 말이에요.

phrases.example: 다음 주까지 전과 신청을 해야 해요.
phrases.en: I have to apply for a change of major by next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교에 정식으로 신청할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for formally applying to the school.

phrases.example: 적성에 안 맞아서 과를 바꾸고 싶어요.
phrases.en: It doesn't suit me, so I want to change my department.
phrases.nuance_ko: '전과하다'를 풀어서 말한 쉬운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier, spelled-out way to say 전과하다.

phrases.en: I decided to change my major.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학과보다 공부 분야 자체를 바꾼다는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels like changing the field of study itself, not just the department.

explain_en: It means switching from one university department to another. You can also say 과를 바꾸다. 전공을 바꾸다 stresses changing the field of study, while 전과하다 feels like the official application process. Do not confuse it with 전과 meaning a criminal record, which is a different word.

examples.en: The two companies formed a partnership.

examples.ko: 우리 학교는 해외 대학과 제휴하고 있어요.
examples.en: Our school has a partnership with overseas universities.
You get a discount if you use the partner card.
News of a new partnership appeared in the news.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 여러 앱과 제휴해서 포인트를 줘요.
examples.en: That shop partners with several apps and gives points.
The partnership ended, so the discount is gone.

explain: 회사나 기관이 서로 도우려고 약속을 맺을 때 써요. '제휴를 맺다', '제휴하다'처럼 같이 써요. '협력'은 함께 일하는 일반적인 말이고, '제휴'는 공식적인 관계라는 느낌이 있어요. '제휴 카드', '제휴 할인'처럼 생활에서도 많이 봐요.

phrases.example: 이 카드를 쓰면 제휴 할인을 받을 수 있어요.
phrases.en: If you use this card, you can get a partner discount.
phrases.nuance_ko: 함께 약속을 맺은 회사에서 받는 할인을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A discount you get from a company that has a partnership agreement.

phrases.en: I made a partner card for the movie theater.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 회사가 함께 만든 카드를 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a card made jointly by two companies.

phrases.en: This is our company's partner company.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-사'는 회사를 뜻하므로 '제휴사'는 제휴한 회사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-사' means company, so '제휴사' is a company one has partnered with.

explain_en: It is used when companies or organizations make an agreement to help each other, as in '제휴를 맺다' or '제휴하다'. 협력 is the general word for working together; 제휴 feels like an official relationship. You also see it in daily life in '제휴 카드' and '제휴 할인'.

t90.ax: The two companies formed a partnership.

en: to be progressed; to be advanced

examples.en: The construction is progressing as scheduled.
I'm worried because the work isn't progressing well.
I'll let you know right away if the negotiation moves forward.
The project made a lot of progress this week.
I can feel my thesis moving forward little by little.
I reported the progress to the team leader.

explain: 공사, 협상, 연구처럼 시간이 걸리는 일이 앞으로 나아갈 때 써요. '진척이 없다', '진척이 더디다'처럼 부정적인 말과 같이 나올 때가 많아요. 사람이 실력이 느는 건 '발전하다'나 '늘다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The research has made no progress for months.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 앞으로 나아가지 않을 때 '진척되다' 대신 쓰는 흔한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common way to say a task is going nowhere, instead of using the verb.

phrases.en: The negotiations are progressing slowly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 나아가긴 하지만 느릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when work is moving forward but slowly.

phrases.en: Thanks to the meeting, the work moved forward a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 긍정적인 상황에서 '많이', '꽤'와 함께 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: In positive situations it pairs well with words like 많이 or 꽤.

explain_en: It is used when a job that takes time, like construction, negotiation, or research, moves forward. It often appears in negative phrases such as '진척이 없다' (no progress) or '진척이 더디다' (progress is slow). When a person improves, use '발전하다' or '늘다'.

t90.ax: I reported the progress to the team leader.

examples.en: Please write your residential address on the form.
This neighborhood is popular as a place to live.
You have to report it when your residence changes.

examples.ko: 저는 회사와 가까운 곳으로 거주지를 옮겼어요.
examples.en: I moved my residence to a place near the company.
Most students' residences are near the school.
Near the park is quiet, so it's good for living.

explain: '거주지'는 사람이 실제로 사는 곳이에요. 일상에서는 '사는 곳'이나 '집'이라고 하고, 서류에서는 '거주지'나 '주소'라고 써요. 회사 위치는 '소재지'라서 사람과 기관에 쓰는 말이 달라요.

phrases.en: I moved my place of residence because of work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이사해서 사는 곳을 바꿀 때 격식 있게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal way to say you changed where you live.

phrases.example: 거주지 변경은 주민센터에서 할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can change your residence at the community center.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류나 행정 일에서 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in paperwork and administration.

phrases.en: Excuse me, where is your place of residence?
phrases.nuance_ko: 사는 곳을 공손하게 물을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to ask where someone lives.

explain_en: 거주지 is where a person actually lives. In daily talk people say 사는 곳 or 집, while forms use 거주지 or 주소. A company's location is 소재지, so the word differs for people and for institutions.

t90.ax: Most students' residences are near the school.

examples.en: My coworker dumped his work on me.

examples.ko: 귀찮은 일을 신입에게 떠맡기면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't foist annoying work onto the newcomer.
She left the child with Grandmother and went out.
Why are you pushing all the responsibility onto me?
The team leader suddenly handed the presentation off to me.

examples.ko: 남에게 떠맡기듯이 일하지 말고 직접 해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't work as if you're dumping things on others; try doing it yourself.

explain: 하기 싫거나 부담스러운 일·책임을 억지로 남에게 넘길 때 써요. 받는 쪽에서 말하면 '떠맡다'가 되니까 짝으로 외워 두세요. 대개 불만이나 비판의 느낌이 들어 있어요.

phrases.en: The person who made the mistake pushed the blame onto me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 책임을 억지로 남에게 넘길 때 써요. 불만의 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when forcing your own responsibility onto someone else, with a tone of complaint.

phrases.en: Please don't dump only the hard work on me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부탁이나 항의할 때 쓰는 부정 명령형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative request form used to ask or protest politely.

phrases.en: They dumped the child on me and left.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이나 사람을 남에게 넘기고 떠나는 모습을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes leaving after handing off a task or person to someone.
phrases.en_equiv: to dump on someone and leave

explain_en: Use it when you force an unwanted job or responsibility onto someone else. From the receiver's side the word becomes '떠맡다', so learn them as a pair. It usually carries a feeling of complaint or criticism.

t90.ax: My coworker dumped his work on me.

examples.en: The referee gave the player a red card.
A player who gets a red card is sent off right away.
A red card came out for a rough foul.
Two yellow cards are the same as a red card.
We lost today's match because of a red card.
That player was sent off with a red card.

explain: 축구 같은 경기에서 반칙을 크게 했을 때 심판이 꺼내는 카드로, 받으면 퇴장해요. 가벼운 경고는 '옐로카드'라고 해요. 보통 '레드카드를 받다', '레드카드를 꺼내다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: That player received a red card for a foul.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반칙한 선수가 퇴장당할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for a player being sent off for a foul.

phrases.en: The referee pulled out the red card right away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 심판의 입장에서 카드를 보여 주는 행동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the action from the referee's side.
phrases.en_equiv: to pull out a red card

phrases.en: You get a yellow card for a minor foul.
phrases.nuance_ko: 레드카드보다 가벼운 경고 카드로, 함께 알아 두면 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: A lighter warning card than the red card; useful to learn together.

explain_en: In sports like soccer, this is the card a referee shows for a serious foul, and the player must leave. A lighter warning is a '옐로카드'. It is usually said as '레드카드를 받다' or '레드카드를 꺼내다'.

en: to lodge temporarily; to stay at someone's home

examples.en: On Jeju Island I stayed at a small private guesthouse.
This summer I will stay at a seaside guesthouse.

examples.ko: 호텔보다 시골집에 민박하는 게 더 좋아요.
examples.en: I like staying at a country house better than a hotel.
After hiking, we stayed overnight at a village guesthouse.
The landlady gave breakfast to the guests staying overnight.

examples.ko: 예약 없이 민박하려고 했는데 방이 없었어요.
examples.en: I tried to stay without a reservation, but there was no room.

explain: 일반 가정집이나 작은 집에서 돈을 내고 하룻밤 자는 것을 말해요. 호텔이나 모텔 같은 숙박업소와 다르게 주인이 사는 집인 경우가 많아요. '펜션'은 가족 단위로 빌리는 별장 느낌이라 달라요.

phrases.en: I'm planning to stay at a homestay on this vacation.
phrases.nuance_ko: '민박하다'와 뜻이 같지만 '을/를 하다' 형태로 계획을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '민박하다', often used when talking about plans.

phrases.en: I stayed two nights at a guesthouse by the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: '민박집'은 묵는 장소를 가리키고, '묵다'와 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '민박집' names the place you stay, and it pairs often with '묵다'.
phrases.en_equiv: to stay at a homestay house

phrases.en: I'd rather stay at a homestay than a hotel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원하는 것을 말하는 활용형이에요. 여행 계획을 이야기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A conjugated form for saying what you want, useful in travel talk.
phrases.en_equiv: I want to stay at a homestay

explain_en: It means paying to sleep a night in an ordinary home or small house. Unlike a hotel or motel, the owner often lives there. A 펜션 feels like a rented villa for families, which is different.

examples.en: My grandmother wove a basket out of wheat straw.
In summer, I go out to the field wearing a straw hat.

examples.ko: 밀짚 가방은 여름 바다에 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: A straw bag goes well with the summer sea.

examples.ko: 마당에 밀짚을 깔고 말린 고추를 널었어요.
examples.en: We spread straw in the yard and laid out the dried peppers.

examples.ko: 밀짚 냄새를 맡으니 어릴 때 시골이 생각났어요.
examples.en: The smell of straw reminded me of the countryside from my childhood.

examples.ko: 시골 체험에서 밀짚 인형을 만들어 봤어요.
examples.en: At the countryside experience program, I made a straw doll.

explain: 밀을 거두고 남은 줄기를 말려 만든 것이에요. 일상에서는 '밀짚모자'로 가장 많이 만나요. 음료를 마시는 '빨대'와 헷갈리지 마세요.

phrases.en: I went to the beach wearing a straw hat.
phrases.nuance_ko: '밀짚'이 들어간 말 중에서 가장 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most common word that contains 밀짚.

phrases.en: I put the fruit in a straw basket.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밀짚으로 엮은 생활용품을 말할 때 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this for everyday items woven from wheat straw.

explain_en: It is the dried stalk left after wheat is harvested. In daily life you most often meet it in '밀짚모자' (straw hat). Don't confuse it with '빨대', the drinking straw.

en: with a scratching sound; with scrape

examples.en: My arm was itchy, so I scratched it hard.

examples.ko: 빨래에 묻은 얼룩을 벅벅 문질러 닦았어요.
examples.en: I scrubbed the stain on the laundry hard to clean it.

examples.ko: 개가 문을 벅벅 긁는 소리가 들려요.
examples.en: I can hear the dog scratching at the door.
The child scrubbed his hair vigorously and came out.
I'm upset because the cat keeps scratching the sofa.

examples.ko: 그는 졸린 얼굴을 손으로 벅벅 비볐어요.
examples.en: He rubbed his sleepy face hard with his hands.

explain: 거칠고 힘주어 긁거나 문지를 때 쓰는 말이에요. '박박'과 비슷하지만 소리가 더 굵게 들려요. 보통 '벅벅 긁다', '벅벅 문지르다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I scrubbed my shoes hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘을 주어 거칠게 닦는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes wiping or scrubbing roughly with force.

phrases.en: I scrubbed my hands vigorously.
phrases.nuance_ko: 때를 없애려고 세게 씻을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when washing hard to remove dirt.

phrases.en: I scrubbed the pot hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: '벅벅'과 비슷하지만 소리가 더 가볍고 높아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 벅벅 but with a lighter, higher sound.

explain_en: It is used for scratching or rubbing roughly and with force. It is similar to '박박' but sounds deeper and heavier. It usually appears as '벅벅 긁다' or '벅벅 문지르다'.

t90.ax: My arm was itchy, so I scratched it hard.

examples.ko: 물이 빠진 갯벌에서 비릿한 냄새가 풍겨 왔어요.
examples.en: A slightly fishy smell drifted from the mudflat after the water went out.

examples.ko: 시장 생선 가게 앞은 비릿해서 코를 막았어요.
examples.en: The area in front of the fish shop at the market was fishy, so I covered my nose.
I touched fish and my hands still smell a bit fishy.
The clams may not have been fresh; my mouth tasted fishy.
If it tastes fishy, try squeezing some lemon on it.

examples.ko: 생선이 오래돼서 냄새가 비릿하지 않나 확인했어요.
examples.en: The fish was old, so I checked whether it smelled fishy.

explain: 생선, 피, 갯벌 같은 데서 나는 날 냄새를 말해요. '비린내'가 명사이고 '비릿하다'는 약간 비린 듯하다는 느낌이에요. 냄새뿐 아니라 입안의 맛에도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: There's a fishy smell coming from the fish shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 냄새를 꾸며 주는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic collocation for describing a smell.

phrases.en: My hands smelled fishy, so I kept washing them.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '비린내'로 말할 때는 '비릿하다'보다 더 직접적으로 느껴져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Using the noun '비린내' feels more direct than '비릿하다'.

phrases.example: 굴에서 비릿한 맛이 나서 잘 못 먹어요.
phrases.en: Oysters have a fishy taste, so I can't eat them well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 냄새뿐 아니라 입안의 맛에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can describe taste in the mouth as well as smell.

explain_en: It describes the raw smell that comes from fish, blood, or mudflats. '비린내' is the noun, and '비릿하다' means slightly fishy. It can describe taste in the mouth as well as smell.
